messages:
OncallBot: paging @oncall — high memory alerts from kv-cache pool on prod-gpu-3, >90% gpu mem across multiple pods, auto-escalation.

AlexW: seeing OOMs + CUDA allocation failures in the runtime logs, looks like fragmentation not raw alloc demand. stack traces show `pytorch/cuda_malloc` returning nullptr.

Priya: confirmed spikes started ~2891234400, correlates with a traffic pattern change to /generate-chat on model xg-large. 500s up ~12m ago.

Santiago: metrics: kv-cache size surged from 6GB to 18GB on some hosts due to continuous batching prefilling large prefixes. eviction_rate dropped while occupancy climbed.

Maria: customer impact: ~3 paying customers on dedicated capacity experiencing latency spikes and a few requests failing with 502. CS alerted.

AlexW: copying logs fragment: ```
[ERR] cudaMalloc failed, tried 2.1GB -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[INFO] arena_free: found fragmented free blocks: 128B..1MB holes, total free=1.3GB, largest_contiguous=64MB
[WARN] kv_cache_insert: prefix_cache grew past soft_limit=12GB, disable_prefetch=false
```

Priya: quick mitigation proposal: 1) disable continuous batching/prefetch on affected router, 2) force arena compaction on nodes, 3) reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096->1024 for model variant, 4) soft-restart pods in a rolling fashion to reclaim fragmented memory. thoughts?

Santiago: +1. Also propose setting per-request KV cap so single long prompt can't prefill entire cache. we have a runtime flag `--kv-max-prefill-bytes` we can toggle.

OpsLead: escalate to oncall lead @AlexW, prioritize disabling batching first — fastest config flip. Maria, flag CS to tell customers we are mitigating and we expect improvement in 10-15m.

AlexW: doing the config flip now. disabling prefetch/continuous-batching on route `prod/xg-large` in router config. command: ```shell
# update config and reload router
curl -X PATCH https://config-api.internal/routes/prod/xg-large -d '{"continuous_batching": false, "prefetch": false}'
```

DeployBot: router config update queued, rolling reload to 3 nodes.

(OncallBot automated) : Config change detected for route prod/xg-large by AlexW — starting rollout.

Priya: while rollout runs I'm going to push a runtime temp hotfix to cap prefill bytes: `--kv-max-prefill-bytes=524288000` (500MB). That should stop the blowups.

Santiago: also increasing arena_compaction_frequency from 0 to 1 (enable background compaction). patching via runtime flags on nodes: `--arena-compaction=on`.

AlexW: router rollout completed. initial telemetry: per-pod kv-cache allocation rates dropping ~70% in 90s. pods showing freed memory.

Maria: CS update sent: "We are seeing improvements, we've applied temporary mitigations and will follow up with root cause and timeline for a permanent fix." Customer response: appreciative, asking if dedicated capacity will be impacted longer term.

DeployBot: pushed runtime flag changes to 4/6 affected GPUs, remaining 2 in progress.

Santiago: note: compaction is memory-expensive while it runs — doing it gradually. watching cudaMalloc errors.

Priya: rolling restart started for pods with >80% fragmentation to force arena reset. command: ```shell
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod --selector=kv_pool=highfrag
```

AlexW: restarted 2 pods, they came up healthy. memory fragment numbers down: largest_contiguous now 1.1GB on restarted hosts.

OncallBot: alert suppression: we silenced the high-mem paging for prod-gpu-3 for 30m while mitigations run.

Santiago: telemetry after fixset: error rate -> down from 4.6% to 0.3%, p95 latency down ~350ms, kv-cache tail allocations normalized. no new cuda OOMs in last 8m.

OpsLead: good progress. we should still plan a rollback path in case compaction worsens perf. Priya, what exact hotfix will you push to source?

Priya: will land two things in the runtime: 1) enforce `kv_max_prefill_bytes` with default 500MB, 2) add a soft cap eviction policy that favors large contiguous blocks to reduce fragmentation. small PR being reviewed now: `runtime: add-prefill-cap-and-evict-lgblocks`.

AlexW: PR reviewed, we can ship as canary to 10% of runtime nodes in prod. schedule canary in 1h after we confirm stability.

Maria: CS asked for timeline. telling them canary + follow-up in ~1.5h and postmortem within 24h.

Santiago: one more observation — a traffic pattern (large system-generated prompts) caused many simultaneous prefill requests, that's what surfaced the allocator degeneracy. We should add a guard in router to throttle prefill concurrency per-model.

Priya: noted. adding router-side throttle to backlog. config: `max_prefill_concurrency=3` for model variant.

AlexW: handing off oncall to @Santiago for night watch. I’ll stay reachable for rollbacks. switching status to `monitoring`.

Santiago: ack taking over. I'll monitor fragmentation, cuda OOMs, and customer queue. If any regression, escalate back to Alex.

DeployBot: canary rollout scheduled at 2891238165 (in 1h).

OncallBot: Incident: kv-cache fragmentation & batching blowup — mitigated (continuing monitor). Pager closed for now.

Maria: filing quick incident note to ops-incident-log with summary + mitigation steps + CS thread link. Will include affected customers and start time 2891234400, mitigation start 2891234565.

Priya: follow-ups for postmortem: - permanent prefill cap - router prefill concurrency throttle - improve arena compaction heuristics - add telemetry alert for single-request prefill > 200MB - e2e test simulating concurrent prefill load.

Santiago: leaving final runbook action: if fragmentation returns >75% and cuda OOMs resume -> toggle `continuous_batching=false` globally for affected model family, then evacuate pods and run forced arena compaction + restarts.

AlexW: thanks team. closing timeline notes, will write detailed postmortem tomorrow. 

(DeployBot automated): Incident thread closed by OncallBot:2891234565
